title: A recent error term lowered PDO probability forecast scores in a 1981-2025 model test
abstract: We tested whether recent error size improves one-month Pacific Decadal Oscillation prediction ranges beyond seasonal variance. We used fixed NOAA ERSSTv5 PDO and Nino 3.4 tables. Each year used earlier targets to fit a common mean model and two Gaussian variance models. There were 540 test months in 1981-2025. Adding the log of one plus scaled previous error squared gave a mean log score gain of -0.002891 nats per month. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.005295 to -0.000843. Five-year blocks and an ENSO variance control also gave negative intervals. Rolling training and recent-only scoring gave intervals across zero. Central 90% coverage fell from 88.33% to 88.15%. The method slightly reduced primary forecast skill. This does not show that all error-history methods fail or that physical noise has no persistence. Revised data, fitted training residuals, a selected formula and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate scores, a figure and a separate numerical check are included.

display.caption: Recent error size gave a small negative primary probability score gain. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Lower panel shows yearly score gains.

citations.reason: We extend its common mean, annual test calendar and seasonal variance comparison with recent error size. Training begins one year later. We wrote new code and share source observations.
Published prior seasonal mean-response test. Its verified bundle preserves the two exact external source snapshots for reproduction.
Prior sign-dependent PDO mean test informed scope; our test concerns error-size information in variance.
